item.title: Local LLM vulnerability detection and sandboxing on underprovisioned Silicon Part 2 of 3: The Sandboxed Local Agent
item.description: Local LLM vulnerability detection and sandboxing on underprovisioned Silicon, a 3 part series. # Part 2 of 3: The Sandboxed Local Agent # October 1st, 2026 To the code → In part 1 we got our local oMLX server running and had a chat with it. In part 2, we’re going to set up a local open-source agent which can talk to this server for its LLM, and we’re going to sandbox it to the point that we are satisfied that we don’t have to rely on the agentic sandbox and don’t have to read into the motivations of its developers (which might be its agents?

item.title: Local LLM vulnerability detection and sandboxing on underprovisioned Silicon Part 1 of 3: The Server
item.description: Local LLM vulnerability detection and sandboxing on underprovisioned Silicon, a 3 part series. # Part 1 of 3: The Server # August 30th, 2026 To the code → I’m not an agentic booster. The interaction of industry capture, political capture, and environmental and intellectual impacts puts it outside of something I can cheerlead. I do think it is how most code is written now, and it is also a concentration point for global engineering research, which means that it is an obligatory area of knowledge for engineers working in emergent topics, and there is no alternative to getting to grips with the tooling from a security perspective.
